newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MSF wants protection for 52,000 refugees in Congo.
newsitem.headline: MSF wants protection for 52,000 refugees in Congo.

text.p: International medical charity Doctors without Borders (MSF) on Friday called on the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighbouring Rwanda to protect some 52,000 refugees living near their border.
"The situation in the Great Lakes region is a horrible human disaster," MSF field coordinator Stephan Oberreit, just back from Kisangani, eastern Congo (formerly Zaire), told a news conference.
He said that between last April and May, 60 people have died each day. Many live in the forests, are severely malnourished and suffer from dehydration.
"Hundreds of 'living dead' are dying in our arms when they arrive in the hospital tent camps," he said, adding that MSF had found about 5,000 lost children in the forest and along roads.
Oberreit called for the systematic registration of all refugees and their protection against physical violence.
MSF also wants those refugees not suspected of crimes against humanity during the 1994 genocide in Rwanda to be given the right to ask for political asylum.
Since international organisations and aid groups started repatriating Rwandan refugees at the end of April, an estimated 54,000 have been taken back to their country by air.
